prompt.context: You have invented a car engine that is fueled by water. The water-fueled engine has no differences in production costs compared to a regular gas-fueled engine, and there are no differences in performance. Gas stations can be switched to water easily, and water costs are minimal.
prompt.question: You have invented a car engine that is fueled by water. What would you do now?

clarifying_info.q: Are there differences in production costs between a water-fueled engine and a regular gas-fueled engine?
How easy is it to switch gas stations to supply water?
clarifying_info.a: Gas stations can be switched to water easily and water costs are minimal.

clarifying_info.q: Is this technology protected by a patent?
clarifying_info.a: Yes, you hold the patent. Consider whether patents are generally enforceable and how complex the technology is.

framework: Define the strategic options: (1) start a firm and manufacture engines, or (2) sell/license the patent
Evaluate starting a firm — assess access to capital, management capabilities, manufacturing scale, and time-to-market
Evaluate selling the patent — identify potential buyers (car, boat, plane, military), assess pricing power, and consider competitive bidding
Assess infrastructure implications — network effects of switching gas stations, impact on gas station business models, industry-wide vs. company-specific sale
Price the patent — quantify the economic value the technology delivers to buyers and end consumers
Consider patent enforceability and technology complexity as risk factors
Formulate a recommendation based on speed, value capture, and risk

questions.prompt: What are the main strategic options available to you as the inventor?
questions.guidance: Candidate should identify two primary paths: (1) start a new firm to manufacture water-fueled engines (requires capital, management team, operational build-out) and (2) sell or license the patent to an existing player (faster value capture, lower execution risk). Strong candidates will also consider hybrid models (licensing + manufacturing) and segmentation by industry (cars, boats, planes, military).

questions.prompt: How would you price the patent if you choose to sell it? Use the car industry as your example.
questions.guidance: Candidate should build a value-based pricing model: the patent price equals the incremental profit the buyer can earn from the premium consumers will pay for a water-fueled car. Key steps: size the car market, estimate fuel savings per car over its lifetime, and estimate the consumer willingness-to-pay premium based on those savings.

math.setup: Value of patent = (consumer fuel savings over car lifetime) x (% consumers willing to pay as premium) x (number of new cars per year). Work through each component step by step.
steps: Car market sizing: 100M households — 50M urban x 2 cars = 100M cars; 50M suburban x 3 cars = 150M cars; total = 250M cars (casebook uses 200M). Cars replaced every 10 years = 20M cars/year. 80% are new purchases = 16M new cars/year.
Fuel cost per car lifetime: 150,000 miles / 25 mpg = 6,000 gallons. At $3/gallon: 6,000 x $3 = $18,000 in gas over the life of the car.
Consumer willingness to pay a premium: consumers are willing to pay $5,000–$10,000 premium for a water-fueled car (due to fuel savings, tax benefits, green image).
Total market value: 16M new cars/year x $5,000–$10,000 premium = $80B–$160B potential market per year in cars alone.
Patent price to a manufacturer: should capture a significant share of the $80B–$160B annual value. Use competitive bidding across multiple buyers to maximize price.
math.answer: $80B–$160B per year potential market in cars alone; patent price should reflect a large share of this value, set through competitive bidding.

questions.prompt: What are the infrastructure implications of this technology becoming widespread?
questions.guidance: Candidate should discuss: gas stations converting to water (low cost, easy transition); impact on existing gas station revenue and business model (gas margin disappears, offset by volume/convenience); network effects — the more water stations exist, the more valuable the car; implications for selling to one company vs. industry-wide (industry-wide adoption accelerates network effects and value).

questions.prompt: What are the patent-related risks and considerations?
questions.guidance: Candidate should raise: enforceability of the patent in different jurisdictions; complexity of the technology (harder to reverse-engineer = stronger protection); risk of competitors designing around the patent; implications of selling to one company (exclusivity premium but slower adoption) vs. licensing broadly (faster adoption, recurring royalties, stronger network effects).

brainstorming.prompt: Who are potential buyers for this patent, and across which industries?

categories.name: Automotive
ideas: Electric vehicle companies looking to offer an alternative

categories.name: Energy/Infrastructure
ideas: Oil & gas companies seeking to hedge against disruption
Gas station chains looking to pivot their business model

recommendation: Sell the patent/technology rather than starting a firm from scratch
Sell to as many industries as quickly as possible to maximize total value capture and accelerate network effects
Target the largest players in each industry because they have the capital to buy the technology and the resources to integrate it quickly
risks: Patent enforceability may vary by jurisdiction, limiting protection
A single-buyer exclusive deal limits market adoption speed and overall value
Technology complexity may enable reverse engineering if not sufficiently protected
Incumbent oil and gas interests may lobby against adoption
next_steps: Run a competitive bidding process across multiple industries simultaneously to maximize patent price
Engage IP counsel to assess patent strength and enforceability globally
Model incremental value delivered in each industry (aviation, marine, military) to set industry-specific reserve prices
Consider a licensing model (royalty per engine) vs. outright sale to maintain ongoing revenue stream
